headline: The gas pipeline meant to feed Oracle's giant New Mexico data center slipped to February 2027, in a story from August that resurfaced today.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the filing and Bloomberg's report date from 14 Aug 2026, and the item was re-dated without new facts.
importance_line: The slip shows that data centers bringing their own gas power still wait on pipelines and land permits, a risk for Oracle and its partners in New Mexico, though this item is seven weeks old and later events are not in it.
summary: Bloomberg reported on 14 Aug 2026, as relayed by EnergyNow on 3 Oct, that Energy Transfer's Transwestern unit pushed the start of its Green Chile gas pipeline from 15 Aug 2026 to 1 Feb 2027 in a regulatory filing, a six-month delay for the line meant to supply Oracle's proposed $165 billion Project Jupiter data center near the Mexican border; OilPrice adds that New Mexico's State Land Office has repeatedly refused the route across state land and that Oracle told regulators in May that delays could jeopardize the project. The data center is designed to run on up to 2.5 gigawatts of gas-fed fuel cells, so no pipeline means no power.
notes: Re-dated old news: EnergyNow (403 here) carries a 14 Aug 2026 Bloomberg story dated 3 Oct; the Bloomberg link was not obtainable, so the URL is the OilPrice page where the facts were read (its own write-up of the filing). Suggest QA hold-back.
